question: Adobe MTS-2 technical round 2, which opened with a barrage of questions on data types: **in which part of memory are static and global variables stored**, and a **comparison of smart and raw pointers**. A coding follow-up: give **working code where a raw pointer causes a memory leak and a smart pointer fixes it.**
lookingFor: Knowledge of the process memory layout (text, data, bss, heap, stack).
Understanding of C++ ownership and RAII.
Knowing the different smart pointer types and when to use each.
Ability to write a short, correct leak demonstration and its fix.
followUps: Why is make_shared preferred over shared_ptr<T>(new T)?
How can shared_ptr cause a leak, and how does weak_ptr fix it?
What is RAII and how does it relate to exception safety?
What is the rule of three/five?
